newsitem.title: CONGO: Gabon's Ebola death toll rises to 14, WHO says.
newsitem.headline: Gabon's Ebola death toll rises to 14, WHO says.

text.p: An outbreak of the Ebola virus in northern Gabon has killed 14 people from 24 cases, the World Health Organisation said from neighbouring Congo on Monday. The previous toll last Thursday was 12.
The WHO's Africa regional office said that a further 60 people who had come into contact with the Ebola victims in the Makokou region of north east Gabon were still under surveillance.

An Ebola outbreak in the same Ogooue-Ivindo province in February killed 21 out of 37 victims. Officials blamed that outbreak on victims eating ape meat, advising people to avoid all but freshly killed monkey meat.
The first victim in the latest outbreak was a hunter suspected to have caught the virus in the forest. He died on August 23 in a hospital at Boue, east of the capital Libreville.
The Ebola virus induces haemorrhagic fever. It kills up to 80 percent of victims, who bleed to death. Ebola is transmitted by direct contact with blood secretions or body fluids.
The virus struck in Kikwit, Zaire in May 1995, killing 245 people. A single victim in Ivory Coast last December survived.
